items.q: What should you remember about **Living vs cadaver**?
items.a: **same structures; difference is** energy flow stops at death.

items.q: What should you remember about **Emotions = energy in motion**?
items.a: **we perceive deltas in energy, not absolute levels.**

items.q: What should you remember about **Mito-centric biology**?
items.a: **genetically identical mice differ in anxiety** partly via mitochondrial energetics; genes identical across cells but mitotypes differ by organ.

items.q: What should you remember about **Eat + breathe for mitochondria**?
items.a: **oxygen and food electrons converge** in mitochondria; they make water and release CO₂, closing the photosynthesis cycle.

items.q: What should you remember about **Social mitochondria**?
items.a: **fusion/fission, division of labor** within cells (subsarcomeric vs intermyofibrillar), lifecycle like ant colonies.
not lack of input energy but **dysfunctional transformation** and distribution.
**energy directed to an organ/brain circuit** builds mitochondrial capacity there; finite budget creates trade-offs (amenorrhea, overtraining, sick behavior).

items.q: What should you remember about **Sickness behavior**?
items.a: **immune system expands energy share;** body conserves via pain, cold, anorexia, apathy (~10–15% digestion cost saved).

items.q: What should you remember about **Aging cliffs**?
items.a: **non-linear mitochondrial decline at life stages; stress/inflammation accelerate.**
**inflammation as energetic state**; cytokines as cellular distress signals when energy flow stalls (hypoxia analog).

items.q: What should you remember about **NAD developmental pace**?
items.a: **faster mitochondrial metabolism →** faster development/shorter lifespan (mouse vs human stem-cell studies).
